claim_rule: Two Holm families over the reference-against-each pairs, flat inconsistency and the kappa difference; 'more consistent' only when both are significant in the policy's favour (an intersection-union test, so no correction across the two)

decomposition.orientation: cell(reference, reference) - cell(member, member), split into judgment and reference parts

lines: The family is named on the command line: reference base (Qwen3-8B), members pick (GRPO (checkpoint-300)). Its arms come from these campaign roots: artifact://sampling/fig5-grpo-v2-fp32-2026-09-26-checkpoint-200-pop-a22af097 (campaign fig5-grpo-v2-fp32-2026-09-26, commit 57bfa3dc8b77, sources 47d982a23576: base); artifact://sampling/fig5-qwen-mix-2026-10-11-checkpoint-300-pop-a22af097 (campaign fig5-qwen-mix-2026-10-11-checkpoint-300, commit 57bfa3dc8b77, sources 47d982a23576: pick).

Checked across the arms: one condition identity but the weights served and the policy labels (judge Qwen3-8B, prompt forced-grpo, label rule lenient, label_only validity with strict_think on, temperature 1.0, truncation model_default, token cap 32768, ruleset openai_rules_all.jsonl (a99062f00a9f...), evaluation mode both, judge type No_Interpretation, rule context isolated, serving dtype float32); one scenario manifest (a22af097639c...) of 500 scenarios; one design (5 decoder draws, 20 semantic attempts, component retry, bootstrap 10,000 at seed 16, randomization 100,000 permutations); one engine (vLLM 0.28.0+cu129, torch 2.13.0+cu129, transformers 5.17.0, TP 1); every root complete and final; no two arms on one set of weights.

Each member serves a merged checkpoint named by its weights digest (pick 9cbc91ce67ad...), whose merge manifest -- the one its draws recorded -- records base weights 668868d5ab4d... from a directory named Qwen3-8B. The reference base serves the upstream directory Qwen3-8B, named by that directory alone (its condition identity carries no content digest): this readout checks the name, not that the reference's files are those weights.

The reference arm base comes from artifact://sampling/fig5-grpo-v2-fp32-2026-09-26-checkpoint-200-pop-a22af097; paired with it by (scenario, decoder draw index) over the one scenario manifest, from another root: pick.
Holm runs within each family (flat inconsistency, the kappa difference) over the members named here (pick): a family of 1, over which each member's Holm p is taken.

Each arm's flat-rate interval is the joint scenario-cluster bootstrap over the arms named here, as one root holding them would give it. Past the bootstrap's first chunk of replicates it depends on which conditions are analysed together, so it can differ in its last digits from the interval its own root's estimates give, which analysed that root's conditions together (artifact://sampling/fig5-grpo-v2-fp32-2026-09-26-checkpoint-200-pop-a22af097: Qwen3-8B/figure5/base, Qwen3-8B/figure5/grpo; artifact://sampling/fig5-qwen-mix-2026-10-11-checkpoint-300-pop-a22af097: Qwen3-8B/figure5/pick). The point estimates, and each contrast's estimate, interval and unadjusted p, do not depend on it.
The yes-shift baseline beside each member is descriptive: no test, in no family; its interval holds p at its point value.
Each GRPO policy arm (pick) is its checkpoint merged into the Qwen3-8B weights in fp32 and served in fp32.

Every arm runs on one fp32 engine: vLLM 0.28.0+cu129, dtype float32, attention backend TRITON_ATTN with Triton's default precision for fp32 dot products (TF32; TRITON_F32_DEFAULT unset), fp32 GEMMs at VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=highest; only the weights differ between arms.

Parity B (HF-PEFT in fp32 against the merged checkpoint served in fp32, in prefill and decode arms), a merge check expected at about 1 and gated at rho >= 0.99 where its 95% interval's half-width is at most 0.01: pick: prefill rho = 1.0003 [0.9998, 1.0009], decode rho = 1.0005 [1.0003, 1.0008].
The base arm (base: Qwen3-8B with no adapter) is served in fp32 on vLLM 0.28.0+cu129; it is not the bf16 Qwen3-8B of the ruleset-size experiment (vLLM 0.19, naive-rules-above prompt).

Training sampled its rollouts from TRL's bf16 colocated engine, a rounded copy of the policy, with token-level importance sampling. The evaluation measures the merged policy itself, not that engine's copy.

yes_shift_definition: Descriptive, no test and in no Holm family. On the reference's cells (scenario x decoder draw): F its full-set judgment, M its per-rule max (phi: no 0, unsure 0.5, yes 1), a cell inconsistent iff phi(F) != M (the separate-call rate's stored contradiction); y_ref and y_mem the two arms' full-set yes shares. p = (y_mem - y_ref) / (1 - y_ref) is the share of the reference's non-yes judgments that would have to turn yes to reach the member's yes share. The shifted rate is the reference's expected inconsistency had each of its non-yes judgments turned yes with probability p, blind to the rules: the mean over its cells of I(phi(F) != M) where F is yes, else p * I(M != yes) + (1 - p) * I(phi(F) != M) (analytic, no simulation). The share of the gain it explains is (rate_ref - shifted) / (rate_ref - rate_mem). Not applicable when the member's yes share is not above the reference's, or its rate is not below. The interval is a scenario-cluster bootstrap of the shifted rate at the campaigns' settings with p held at its point value (p's own sampling variation is not propagated).
